newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha says will not share power.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha says will not share power.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha said on Wednesday he would not remain in office indefinitely alongside a leftist government, but did not say explicitly if and when he would step down.
Speaking three days after a general election which the Socialist Party appears to have won, Berisha told a news conference: "There will be no cohabitation."

Berisha said he would abide by statements he made during the election campaign, a reference to his pledges to step down if his Democratic Party lost power to the Socialist opposition. But he declined to say when and how he might step down.
"I have to keep to what I said. And there will be no wavering in that respect...but in the most appropriate way for this country," he said in English.

Berisha said he had asked Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to propose an interior minister to replace Belul Celo, who he said had left the country. He said under a March agreement to set up a multi-party government and stage last Sunday's election the appointee had to be from his Democratic Party.

A confrontation had erupted earlier on Wednesday between the two men over control of the interior ministry, which is responsible for the security forces. Fino accused Berisha of interfering by trying to appoint another of his loyalists even though Celo was still in office.
